summary: The theorem and proof are correct as stated. For each singleton affine subspace A={z}, the only nonempty admissible index set is {z}; all masses are at most a_z, while t_z=a_z with center z has nonempty full-mass metronoid core and vacuous relative halfspace conditions, so G_A^rel=a_z. With r=0 and W_A=a_z, part (22) of accepted fact 3d1f63abf09b2abb gives G at least min{(W+a_z)/2, 2^n a_z}; since G<W/2 makes the first entry greater than G, this forces a_z<=2^{-n}G. This yields the claimed exceptional-fiber mass bound and, together with the exact free matching formula, the saturation and empty-core conclusions for every maximum matching. The half-metronoid cap-loss estimate follows with the correct normalization from central symmetry and the negative first-moment bound. Its fiberwise application correctly handles zero slack, exceptional fibers, and the far-contact complement. The saturated quadruple family is nonempty, every relevant cap lies in the descendant collection, and the epsilon argument correctly handles a nonattained infimum without assuming attainment of either optimization. The asymptotic, quantitative, and converse consequences follow with the stated constants and quantifiers.
